version.changelog:
- Removed the file: skill-card.md
- No functional or user-facing changes; this update only deletes redundant documentation.

llm.summary: This skill connects to a Kia account to read vehicle information and issue user-confirmed vehicle commands, with the sensitive behavior clearly disclosed.

dimensions.detail: The skill needs Kia credentials, account session state, and vehicle location/control access for its purpose; this is sensitive but proportionate to remote vehicle management.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses an MCP configuration entry that runs the external npm package via npx; this is disclosed, but users should understand they are trusting that package source and future package resolution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions emphasize listing vehicles first, not guessing keys, stopping on failed login, not exposing secrets, and requiring confirmation for writes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill states that a remember-me token is stored locally and can refresh sessions silently forever, with a documented confirmation-gated forget-session tool and warnings around token export.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capability is high impact because it can access vehicle status, location, EV charging, climate, and lock/unlock controls, but those are the stated purpose of the skill and are described directly.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving an MCP server access to your Kia account, vehicle location, and remote vehicle commands. Keep `KIA_WRITE_MODE` at `none` for read-only use, avoid exporting the refresh token unless needed for a deployment, and use `kia_forget_session` if you no longer want the machine to retain access.
llm.findings: [AS2] expected: The flagged `.mcp.json`/`~/.claude/mcp.json` text is a setup instruction for registering this MCP server, not an instruction to read or enumerate existing MCP configurations; I downgraded it as disclosed installation guidance rather than agent snooping.
